changes: No substantive changes; persons, roles, date and era confirmed.

Notes expanded: the direct-order reading 794 (1674 CE) is flagged as a real possibility, given the catalogue's reading and the generally late dating of the Nepālamāhātmya; the weekday could settle it.

date.as_written: munirandhai samudraiśca, yute nepālavatsare | bhādra ca sitapakṣetu, dvitīyāyāṃ ravaudine

notes: The chronogram is muni (7), randhra (9), samudra (4). Under the standard rule aṅkānāṃ vāmato gatiḥ it reads 497, i.e. NS 497 = 1377 CE (Bhādrapada falls in Aug–Sep 1377). The catalogue reads the digits in direct order as 794(!), i.e. 1674 CE. Scribes sometimes did write chronograms in direct order. A 1377 copy of the Skandapurāṇa Nepālamāhātmya would be unusually early, which makes the 794 reading worth taking seriously. Checking whether Bhādrapada śukla 2 fell on a Sunday in NS 497 or in NS 794 should decide it. The text is 'nepāla mahimā', i.e. the Nepālamāhātmya. 'likhet' is an optative used with past meaning.
